answer.recommendation: Order 3 boxes of compatible tips (standard or low-retention; 3,000 tips total). Base need is 24 experiments x 80 tips = 1,920 tips. Adding the 10% reserve gives 1,920 x 1.10 = 2,112 tips. At 1,000 tips per box, that rounds up to 3 boxes, leaving about 888 tips spare after the reserve.
quality_notes: Arithmetic: 24 x 80 = 1,920 base tips; 10% reserve = 192; total required = 2,112; boxes = ceil(2,112 / 1,000) = 3.
The reserve is applied to the base requirement and the box count is rounded up, so the order does not fall short.

I did not have access to the visible experiment plan beyond the work packet, so the quantities come only from the packet values. Any plan detail that changes experiment count, tips per experiment, or the reserve would change the order.
The packet lists two compatible tip types but does not say which one to use. Either is acceptable per the packet; the choice is left to the buyer.
I did not contact colleagues and received no approvals; the recommendation is based solely on the packet.
